| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit read; figures go within the text file, captions in the text file; online colour is free |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the aims page says the journal is "not an advocate of any one trend or school" but is "especially committed" to phenomenology and contemporary continental philosophy, and invites work on points of intersection between the continental European and Anglo-American traditions (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/aims-and-scope, snapshot 2025-12-04). The Crossref sample of 2026 is consistent: a special issue on sedimentation in Husserlian phenomenology (DOI 10.1007/s11007-026-09744-3), a paper on Kojève and science (10.1007/s11007-026-09739-0), Merleau-Ponty on the institution of nature (10.1007/s11007-026-09727-4). The earlier pass also noted a 2025 Bergson special issue, retained as an earlier AI-research observation.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** phenomenological analysis; interpretation of texts of continental thinkers; historical-genealogical argument; comparative work across the continental and Anglo-American traditions (stated on the aims page); extended review articles ("considerable space" for reviews, same page).

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Scope statement: the aims page says the journal is "not an advocate of any one trend or school" and is committed to phenomenology and contemporary continental philosophy (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/aims-and-scope, snapshot 2025-12-04). No political stance is stated.
- Named thinkers in titles/abstracts of 88 articles with abstracts, 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23; small base, so each count is a lower bound): Husserl 23 (26.1%), Heidegger 12 (13.6%), Merleau-Ponty 9 (10.2%), Hegel 8 (9.1%), Beauvoir 6 (6.8%), Kant 5 (5.7%), Derrida 4 (4.5%), Arendt 3 (3.4%), Nietzsche 3 (3.4%), Agamben 3 (3.4%), Sartre 2 (2.3%), Gadamer 2 (2.3%), Foucault 1 (1.1%), Levinas 1 (1.1%), Wittgenstein 1 (1.1%).
- Traditions and terms: "phenomenolog*" 48 (54.5%), "critique" 14 (15.9%), "analytic" 7 (8.0%), "continental" 4 (4.5%), "existential*" 4 (4.5%), "critical theor*" 3 (3.4%), "hermeneut*" 2 (2.3%), "feminis*" 1 (1.1%), "postcolon*|decolon*|colonial" 1 (1.1%).
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Phenomenology and Existential Philosophy 503 articles, Philosophy, Ethics, and Existentialism 416, Critical Theory and Philosophy 135.
- Editorial board: names listed at https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/editorial-board (snapshot 2025-12-04) include Dan Zahavi, Steven Crowell, Sara Heinämaa, Natalie Depraz, Linda Alcoff and Lewis Gordon; the page states no school preference of its own.
- Reading of the counts: phenomenology, and Husserl above all, is the dominant frame in the abstracts; post-Kantian, French and Heideggerian authors follow; critical-theory and postcolonial vocabulary is rare (1-3% in a base of 88). This describes what is published, not an editorial stance on any political question.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: no framing rule on the guidelines page; the aims page defines the journal's focus as phenomenology and contemporary continental philosophy, with interest in continental and Anglo-American intersections (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/aims-and-scope, snapshot 2025-12-04).
- Article types: essays on "expressly theoretical topics" and practical socio-political problems, plus review articles with "considerable space" (same page).
- Length: 7,000-9,000 words including references and footnotes (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/submission-guidelines, snapshot 2025-12-05).
- Argument frame in the sample: "argu*" in 44 of 88 abstracts (50.0%), "this article/paper/essay" in 63 (71.6%); five of the ten most recent abstracts start with "This paper/article/introduction" (Crossref, 2026).
- Consequence of ignoring the scope: none stated on the pages read; no desk-reject rate is published (SciRev: 0 reviews).

### Methodological Preferences

Scoring rule (this pass's own convention, not a journal statement): hits divided by the 88 records with abstracts; 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need an editorial statement; none was found beyond the aims page naming phenomenology as a commitment, which names a tradition and not a method score. ### Voice & Style

- Abstract: 150-250 words; 4-6 keywords (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/submission-guidelines, snapshot 2025-12-05).
- Format: citations by footnote with an author-year reference list; footnotes rather than endnotes; decimal headings of at most three levels; Word or LaTeX (same page).
- First-person use in the 88 deposited abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23): "I" appears in 44 (50.0%), "we" in 30 (34.1%), "our" in 12 (13.6%), "my" in 11 (12.5%); "this article/paper/essay" in 63 (71.6%). Example: "I show that he arrives at a conception of unconscious life" (DOI 10.1007/s11007-026-09753-2) and "I aim to show that Kojève's rejection of the classical conception of Being" (DOI 10.1007/s11007-026-09739-0).
- Ten most recent abstract openings sampled (Crossref, 2026): five begin with "This paper/article/introduction" (DOIs 10.1007/s11007-026-09743-4, 10.1007/s11007-026-09744-3, 10.1007/s11007-026-09727-4, 10.1007/s11007-026-09739-0, 10.1007/s11007-026-09729-2); the other five open with a general statement about phenomenology or a concept (10.1007/s11007-026-09753-2, 10.1007/s11007-026-09737-2), a reply to a book (10.1007/s11007-026-09748-z), "Building on the Husserlian discourse" (10.1007/s11007-026-09732-7) or "In contrast to the early versions" of Husserl's ethics (10.1007/s11007-026-09734-5).

### Practical Concerns

- Ethics / consent: the guidelines ask for a "Compliance with Ethical Standards" section covering funding, competing interests, informed consent for human participants and animal welfare (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/submission-guidelines, snapshot 2025-12-05); the editors may reject non-compliant manuscripts.
- Declarations: author-contribution and competing-interest statements are entered in the submission interface at submission, and declarations missing from a submission lead to it being returned as incomplete (same URL).
- Data: the journal follows Springer Nature's research-data policy and all original research needs a data availability statement; sharing is strongly encouraged (same URL).
- Preprints: allowed at any time, including during review, per the Springer Nature policy (https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing, snapshot 2025-09-06); see the Preprint table.
- OA and charges: hybrid; APC GBP 2,190 / USD 3,090 / EUR 2,490 if OA is chosen, free subscription route (https://link.springer.com/journal/11007/how-to-publish-with-us, snapshot 2025-12-04).
- AI: LLM use to be documented in Methods; copy-editing help exempt (guidelines URL in the AI Policy table).
- Anonymisation: names, affiliations and identifying citations of one's own work must be removed from the manuscript and files; a separate title page carries author details (guidelines URL above).
- Unaffiliated authors: the guidelines say that for authors who are temporarily unaffiliated only city and country of residence are captured, not email unless requested (guidelines URL above). That shows unaffiliated authors are catered for; it is not a statement of acceptance rates for them.

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A non-anonymised manuscript: the journal is double-blind and expects the author to anonymise manuscript and files (Peer Review table; Practical Concerns).
- Work already published or under consideration elsewhere (Manuscript Submission rule on the guidelines page, Practical Concerns).
- Undocumented LLM use beyond copy editing (AI Policy table).

### Soft Tax

- Length target of 7,000-9,000 words including references and footnotes (Format table).
- Footnote-based citation with an author-year reference list and decimal headings, and an abstract of 150-250 words (Format table, Voice & Style).
- Timeline uncertainty: a publisher-stated median of 13 days to first decision (2025 snapshot) sits against two self-reported 2023-2025 rejections at 3.5-4 months (Review Cycle Time); neither is a reliable estimate.

### Best Suited For

- Phenomenological work, especially on Husserl, Heidegger or Merleau-Ponty: "phenomenolog*" appears in 54.5% and Husserl in 26.1% of 88 abstracts (Orientation, Epistemological Leanings).
- Interpretive or historical papers on continental thinkers, with an explicit argument: "interpret*" 23.9%, "histor*|genealog*" 28.4%, "argu*" 50.0% (Methodological Preferences, Framing Requirements).
- Papers bridging continental and Anglo-American traditions: stated as an interest on the aims page (Orientation).

### Not Recommended For

- Empirical or quantitative studies: "empirical" appears in 4.5% and quantitative or ethnographic terms in 0% of 88 abstracts (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity in a small base, not a stated exclusion.
- Work with no continental or phenomenological connection: the aims page states the journal's commitment to that tradition (Framing Requirements); no exclusion rule is stated.
